By Francisco Rodrigues | Edited by Jamie Crawley Oct 17, 2026, 8:00 a.m. EDT 2 min read Make preferred on Share Share this article Copy link X icon X (Twitter) LinkedIn Facebook Email Make preferred on Banks could slow the growth of stablecoins like USDC and USDT by paying more to savers Summary Show A BIS working paper found a 1 basis point rise in U.S. bank deposit rates predicted slower stablecoin growth, cutting ten-week growth from 15% to 12%. The effect was stronger for Circle's USDC than Tether's USDT, which the authors linked to USDC's closer ties to U.S. users. The authors say banks retain some influence over stablecoin adoption through deposit pricing, though the sample covers only one high-rate period.
